is_anopheles.evidence: The study focuses on Anopheles gambiae and Anopheles coluzzii (Anopheles gambiae complex) in Senegal.

reports_target_markers.evidence: The paper reports genotyping for Vgsc L995F (L1014F), Vgsc L995S (L1014S), Vgsc N1575Y (N1575Y), and Ace-1 G280S (G119S) (Page 4, Section 2.7).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: The paper provides genotype counts and frequencies for the markers in Figures 3A, 3B, and 3C, and in the text (e.g., Page 7, Section 3.6).

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected from field sites in Senegal (Tambacounda, Kedougou, Fatick) (Page 3, Section 2.1).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is an original empirical study conducting field collections, bioassays, and molecular genotyping.

sub_country_location.evidence: The study specifies three health districts: Tambacounda, Kedougou, and Fatick (Page 3, Section 2.1).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: The study was conducted during the 2017 and 2018 rainy seasons (Page 3, Section 2.1).

duplicate_risk.evidence: The study describes new field collections from 2017 and 2018.

supplement.evidence: The required genotype data is provided in the main text and figures.

assessment.summary: This study characterizes insecticide resistance in Anopheles gambiae and An. coluzzii populations from three districts in Senegal (Tambacounda, Kedougou, Fatick) collected in 2017-2018. It reports high resistance to pyrethroids and DDT, susceptibility to organophosphates and carbamates (with suspected bendiocarb resistance in Kedougou), and genotypes for kdr (L1014F, L1014S, N1575Y) and Ace-1 (G119S) markers. Metabolic resistance was also investigated via gene expression profiling.
